item.title: 【Singles (lossless)】WAV - Collage "Diana/I'll Be Loving You" Remixes US CD Maxi
item.description:
​

by the start of 1993, freestyle music, which at one time had come to define crossover dance radio in the US, was now no longer considered viable at neither the club or radio level. freestyle artists signed to major labels like george lamond, lisette melendez and safire, were dropped. the other artists who still releasing material were seen as singers championing a genre long past its prime.

it was in the cultural landscape that makes success of new Jersey/south philly based artist or group (depending on who you ask), collage's "i'll be loving you" so fascinating. released in the summer of 1993, on the independent freestyle label metropolitan records, the song utilized the "planet rock" beat, that even by then had been overused. but adam marano's song writing, pop production and vocal (again, depending on you ask), made "i'll be loving you" standout above the fray.

a regional hit in california, texas, and florida (thanks to it's spanish-ish version) before garnering national radio spins, "i'll be loving you" defined the odds reached a peak of #56 on billboard's hot 100 in the march 1994. charting on the hot 100 in freestyle's late 80s and early 90's heyday was an achievement but do to accomplish then where radio had all but turned its back to the freestyle genre made the chart success even more that remarkable.

"gangster of love" was released as the follow-up in 1994 to a tepid response. "diana," my absolute favorite collage song (the original version specifically) was deployed as the collage's third single in early 1995. the release was accompanied by a techno mix of "i'll be loving you" and marked the first time that song appeared on a CD single. but by the then the momentum was lost. what was also happening around this time was the changing sound of freestyle music inspired by planet soul's 1995 top 30 pop hit "set u free."
